page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the 2.8 GHz Ampere Altra processor, with 1 thread per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate CPU and memory capabilities. The instance achieves average performance in stress-ng single-core (1789.99) and multi-core (7136.84) tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, with read speeds of 50.64 GB/sec and write speeds of 29.82 GB/sec, though small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 283.98 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks show mixed results; single-threaded gzip compression is average at 23.76 GB/sec, whereas Passmark CPU encryption is poor at 649.99, and bzip3 decompression is weak.

Given its dedicated Arm-based architecture and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g6r.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads optimized for Arm instruction sets. It is suited for general-purpose applications such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 5.77 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring an average 2947.42 in Passmark database tests. However, its weak performance in Redis SET operations (5.78 million operations/sec) and Passmark memory tests suggests it is less optimal for memory-intensive or high-throughput caching layers.
